title: The weather
description: Say what the weather is like, and how warm it is.

explanation.summary: Spanish talks about the weather with the verb hacer. You do not say “it is hot”, you say “it does hot”. The structure is always hacer followed by a noun: hace calor, hace frío, hace sol, hace viento.

sections.heading: How the weather is built
sections.body: The verb hacer carries the weather, and the noun after it says what the weather is. The whole phrase is a single idea: hace calor is one thing, the same as “it is hot”. In the negative it is no hace calor, and in the past it was hacía calor.

sections.heading: Asking about it
sections.body: To ask, you use the question word qué, and the verb comes before it: ¿Qué tiempo hace? There is also ¿Qué día hace?, which asks what the day is like rather than what the weather is.

sections.heading: Numbers and degrees
sections.body: Temperature is in degrees: hace treinta grados. The number goes straight before grados, with no word in between. The word grados is the same for every number, unlike English, where you say degrees or degree.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: The weather uses hacer, not estar: hace calor, hace frío, hace sol.
Masculine: el sol. It also means sun cream.
